title: Introduction to jQuery Effects
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of introduction to jquery effects in a jQuery application.
Apply the purpose of visual effects in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify built-in effects with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through introduction to jquery effects with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns the purpose of visual effects into a repeatable implementation choice. Built-in effects and .animate() can reveal state changes, but effects should not block interaction or ignore reduced-motion preferences. Prefer CSS transitions for simple visual changes.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
